newsitem.title: USA: GM raises prices average of 1.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: GM raises prices average of 1.3 percent.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Thursday that sticker prices for its carry-over 1998 model cars and trucks will increase by 1.3 percent, the automaker's smallest average price hike in more than a decade.

GM said prices for comparably equipped cars will increase an average of 1.5 percent, while prices for comparably equipped trucks will increase 1.1 percent, both compared with year-end prices for 1997 models.

The increase represents only about 42 models that are largely unchanged from the 1997 model year. It does not include new or redesigned models, including the Oldsmobile Intrigue, Chevrolet Prizm, Chevrolet Corvette Convertible and Cadillac Seville.
Prices for those cars will be announced closer to their introduction.
GM's 1.3 percent average price increase for 1998 compares with 1.7 percent for 1997 models, 2.7 percent for 1996 models and 3.2 percent for 1995 models.

The lower price increases come at a time when the U.S. vehicle market is fiercely competitive, with many Japanese automakers cutting car prices. Nissan Motor Co. Ltd. announced last week the price for the best-selling version of its new 1998 Altima sedan would be $1,500 less than a comparably equipped 1997 model.
Toyota Motor Corp. last year cut the price of its new Camry sedan, which is now the top-selling U.S. passenger car.
GM is not reducing any prices of individual models, but it is keeping two models unchanged -- the Cadillac Catera at $30,635 and the Corvette coupe at $38,060.

GM spokesman Dean Rotondo said GM made its largest price increases on new models and those that are selling well, such as the Chevrolet Venture minivan, which increased 2 percent to a base price of $22,259 for the long-wheelbase, four-door model. The price of the Chevrolet Cavalier is up 2.2 percent to an average of $14,482.
"On the newer models, we felt that we could take a little more price, because the market is demanding" the vehicles, he said.
Ford Motor Co. and Chrysler Corp. are expected to announce similarly low average price increases in August.
